whats_working.title: What’s already working
paragraphs: Eighteen reviews, all five stars, in about **14 months**. That’s a strong foundation, and it’s the hardest part to fake. Clients clearly like working with you.

rows.why_it_helps: Services tell customers and Google exactly what you offer
rows.what_to_do: Add each service you sell, with a one-line description

rows.why_it_helps: Secondary categories describe more of what you do
rows.what_to_do: Add secondary categories that fit your services

rows.why_it_helps: More real photos give clients a better view of your business
rows.what_to_do: Add team, office and work photos until you’re past 10

rows.why_it_helps: Regular posts keep a profile active
rows.what_to_do: Post once a month: a tip, a service update or an offer

rows.finding: No UTM tracking on the website link
rows.why_it_helps: Shows in analytics which visits come from your profile

reviews.title: What we found in the reviews
paragraphs: **Sixteen of the 18 reviews** are star ratings only, with no written text. Two include a few words, and one of those is detailed.
You’ve replied to **one review**. Written reviews matter because both Google and future clients read them to understand what you do.
According to Whitespark’s Local Search Ranking Factors Report, **reviews make up about 20% of local pack ranking** weight.

image.alt: Google reviews for Rocket Boost Virtual Assistants showing five-star ratings with no written text

scan_recommendations.title: What the scan recommends
paragraphs: The scan came back with suggestions for your profile. The word it comes back to most is **reviews.** It points to getting more written reviews as the biggest lever for closing the gap with nearby competitors.

image.alt: Vulnerable competitors from the scan: Alliance Resource Group, Advantex Professional Services, Kforce and DCL Staffing LLC, with their review counts and ratings

strong_review.note: The reviews that tend to help the most do three things: **they name the service, include a photo, and get an owner reply**. Customers can also tap the service they received right in the Google form.

example_images.alt: Example five-star Google review from a small CPA firm that names the service, virtual bookkeeping
Example photo attached to the review: a laptop on a tidy desk showing a video call
Example owner reply thanking the reviewer and mentioning tax season

free_steps.title: Three steps you can take this week
steps: Ask your next few happy clients for a short review that mentions the service they received, such as virtual bookkeeping, and a photo if they’re comfortable.
Reply to your existing reviews. Seventeen are waiting for a thank-you that mentions the service.
Check that your profile’s service list matches what you actually offer.

paragraphs: You already have the hardest part, which is happy clients. The next step is making that visible. When someone in Costa Mesa compares a few firms, the profile that shows **reviews naming the services, real photos, and owners who reply** is easier to trust and easier to choose. In practice that means:
bullets: A profile that shows **what you do, not just a star rating**
A profile that stays active month after month

how_it_works.title: How Biz{{Simpler}} can help RBVA
intro: **BizSimpler** makes that process easier. We send review requests that guide your clients to **pick the service, add a photo and share their experience** in their own words.
We manage the photos, and the client approves every review. **You get a steady flow of reviews that follow the way Google likes it.**
